ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cars A and B travel in the same direction on a straight, level road, and their v-t graph is shown in the figure. It is known that the two cars are side by side at t=30 s. Then at t=0 s, what position is car B in relative to car A? How many meters apart are the two cars?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At t=0 s, car B is 100 m in front of car A.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the v-t graph of cars A and B, with the vertical axis being velocity v (m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis being time t (s). The graph line of car A first rises linearly from t=0, v=0 to t=10 s, v=40 m/s, and then remains horizontal at v=40 m/s until after 30 s. The graph line of car B is a straight line passing through the origin, reaching v=40 m/s at t=20 s, and continuing to rise linearly, so extending according to the graph line to t=30 s, the velocity is 60 m/s. Reasoning: The area under the v-t graph represents displacement. From 0 to 30 s, the displacement of car A is the triangular area of the first 10 s plus the rectangular area of the following 20 s: s_A=1/2×10×40+20×40=200+800=1000 m. The displacement of car B from 0 to 30 s is the triangular area: s_B=1/2×30×60=900 m. Therefore, from 0 to 30 s, car A travels 100 m more than car B. It is known that at t=30 s the two cars are side by side, which indicates that car A caught up with the 100 m difference from car B in these 30 s, so at t=0 s car B was 100 m in front of car A.
